- Experience supporting global stakeholders and facilitating virtual cross-functional work.

- Experience producing standards, playbooks, training or reusable process assets.

- BPM lifecycle, BPMN 2.0, process hierarchy, ownership, E2E analysis, KPI design, variants and controls.

- Practical knowledge of Lean/Six Sigma plus mining, Agile, VSM, journey or digital enablement.

- Signavio, ARIS, Bizagi or similar; Celonis or other mining exposure preferred.

- Strong facilitation, technical writing, analytical structure, global communication and project coordination.

ExxonMobil's state-of-the-art campus north of Houston serves as home to its Upstream, Product Solutions and Low Carbon Solutions businesses and their associated service groups. The facility opened in 2014 and accommodates more than 10,000 employees and visitors.

The campus was constructed to the highest standards of energy efficiency and environmental stewardship. Its design incorporates extensive research into best practices in building and workplace design through extensive benchmarking of the world’s top academic, research, and corporate facilities.

Learn more about what we do in Houston here .

What role you will play in our team

As a Commercial Manager in ExxonMobil’s Midstream Business Development organization, you will be responsible for identifying, developing, and executing commercial opportunities that enhance portfolio value, create market optionality, and support strategic growth objectives across a diverse asset footprint. This role requires developing and maintaining relationships with producers, marketers, refiners, petrochemical companies, midstream service providers, and other industry participants while leading the origination, structuring, negotiation, and execution of complex commercial transactions.

The successful candidate will leverage North American midstream market knowledge, commercial expertise, and relationship management skills to originate opportunities, optimize asset utilization, and support growth across crude oil, natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), refined products, petrochemicals, and related midstream value chains. This position will support a defined commodity-specific portfolio within ExxonMobil’s Midstream Business Development organization, based in Spring, Texas, and will require periodic travel.

What you will do

Business Development

- Identify new business opportunities that leverage and support ExxonMobil’s portfolio volumes and midstream assets.

- Support asset growth by developing midstream commercial strategies and identifying market access and value-maximization opportunities.

- Evaluate market trends, competitive dynamics, and customer requirements to inform commercial decision-making.

- Monitor industry activity and provide insights on opportunities and risks impacting the business.

- Collaborate across ExxonMobil's value chain to identify and evaluate opportunities that enhance portfolio value.

Commercial Development & Contract Management

- Develop, negotiate, and execute commercial agreements consistent with ExxonMobil strategies and objectives.

- Lead negotiations with counterparties to create value-enhancing opportunities across gathering, processing, transportation, storage, terminaling, fractionation, and energy commodity logistics services.

- Manage a portfolio of commercial relationships and agreements while ensuring alignment with business objectives.

Relationship Management

- Develop and maintain strategic relationships with customers, suppliers, market participants, and other industry stakeholders while representing ExxonMobil in the marketplace.

- Create and maintain a strong network of industry contacts to support opportunity generation and market intelligence.

- Collaborate with internal stakeholders across operations, engineering, finance, planning, legal, and commercial organizations to execute business objectives.

About you

- Minimum 10 years of midstream commercial, business development, marketing, trading, or related experience in the oil and gas or petrochemicals industries, along with a Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Finance, Management, Supply Chain, Marketing, or a related discipline.

- Applicants must have excellent collaboration, communication, and interpersonal skills and the ability to deliver results in a performance-driven and team-oriented environment.

- Strong business, financial, and economic analysis capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications/ Experience

- Significant experience in one or more midstream commodity sectors, including crude oil, natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), refined products, petrochemicals, or related energy markets.

- Proven expertise in pipeline gathering, transportation, processing, storage, terminaling, fractionation, or energy commodity logistics services.

- Strong commercial negotiation and contract development experience.

- Established industry relationships with producers, marketers, refiners, petrochemical companies, midstream service providers, or other market participants.

- Strong critical thinking, commercial judgment, and strategic decision-making capabilities.

- Ability to manage multiple complex opportunities simultaneously and prioritize effectively.

- Demonstrated success originating and executing value-creating commercial transactions within the oil and gas midstream sector.

- Strong presentation, influencing, and stakeholder management skills.

- Adaptability and the ability to perform effectively in a changing business environment.

- High commitment to identifying, developing, and capturing new market opportunities.

- Detail-oriented and capable of producing results in time-constrained situations.

- Surveillance Monitoring & Reporting

- Execute daily trade surveillance tasks, including alert reviews and escalation tracking.

- Prepare and distribute routine compliance reports (e.g., position limits, trade activity, sanctions screening).

- Support monthly and quarterly KPI reporting for Trading and Compliance leadership.

- Track and report sanctions-related metrics and compliance status.

- Maintain and update compliance calendars, SharePoint directories, and version-controlled documents.

- Ensure training materials are current and aligned with regulatory requirements and internal policies.

- Support onboarding and refresher training initiatives for trading and support staff.

- Grant, review, and revoke access to compliance systems and data repositories.

- Assist in periodic access audits and ensure alignment with internal control standards.

- Maintain and update Compliance operating processes and documents.

- Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple operational tasks simultaneously.

- Familiarity with trade surveillance tools, sanctions screening systems, and regulatory reporting platforms.

- Experience in managing compliance training programs and tracking performance metrics.

- Proficiency in Excel, SharePoint, and data visualization/reporting tools.

- Ability to distill complex data into clear summaries for leadership.

- Experience in compliance operations, preferably in trading or financial services

- Willing to work from early afternoon to late evening (around 10pm) supporting London trading hours.

- Experience with or knowledge of financial derivative regulatory frameworks

About us

At ExxonMobil, our vision is to lead in energy innovations that advance modern living and a net-zero future. As one of the world’s largest publicly traded energy and chemical companies, we are powered by a unique and diverse workforce fueled by the pride in what we do and what we stand for.

The success of our Upstream, Product Solutions and Low Carbon Solutions businesses is the result of the talent, curiosity and drive of our people. They bring solutions every day to optimize our strategy in energy, chemicals, lubricants and lower-emissions technologies.

We invite you to bring your ideas to ExxonMobil to help create sustainable solutions that improve quality of life and meet society’s evolving needs. Learn more about our What and our Why and how we can work together .

About The Role

About Houston

ExxonMobil's state-of-the-art campus north of Houston serves as home to its Upstream, Product Solutions and Low Carbon Solutions businesses and their associated service groups. The facility opened in 2014 and accommodates more than 10,000 employees and visitors.

By bringing many global functional groups together, the campus provides employees with the tools and capabilities needed today, and in the future, to achieve business objectives and accelerate the discovery of new resources, technologies and products. It was designed to foster improved collaboration, creativity and innovation and enhance the company’s ability to attract, develop and retain the top talent in the industry.

The campus is located in Spring, Texas, on 385 wooded acres immediately to the west of Interstate Highway 45 (I-45), at the intersection of I-45 and the Hardy Toll Road, approximately 25 miles from the cultural vibrancy of downtown Houston.

The campus was constructed to the highest standards of energy efficiency and environmental stewardship. Its design incorporates extensive research into best practices in building and workplace design through extensive benchmarking of the world’s top academic, research, and corporate facilities.

Learn more about what we do in Houston  here .

What Role You Will Play on Our Team

ExxonMobil is seeking qualified and experienced individuals to provide onsite operational expertise for its oil and gas development projects. The primary role and responsibility of the Well Operations Supervisor is to direct and manage well site operations for the ExxonMobil Wells Organization. The Wells Organization executes all wellwork operations (spanning from drilling, completions, to well management), in compliance with internal and external standards. Well management operations include all wellwork post-completion; inclusive of drillouts, remedial workovers, and plug and abandonment. This role works in support of the ExxonMobil Wells Organization to conduct worldwide oil and gas well drilling, completion, and well management operations with an emphasis on safety, cost, and efficiency improvement. You will have the opportunity to travel domestically and internationally, both onshore and offshore to rig-based site locations while working in a team environment and with diverse cultures.

This position is a rotational schedule; you will work on the well site (i.e. drilling rig, frac site, etc.) for two to four weeks (location dependent), then will be off for a corresponding amount of time. On-the-job mentorship as well as formal classroom training will be provided on theories and principles of drilling and well management.

This position is designated safety sensitive and is subject to a background check and drug and alcohol testing as required by ExxonMobil’s Alcohol and Drug Program.

About You

Skills and Qualifications

- 5-15 years' experience working on or managing well sites (drilling rig, frac fleet, workover rig, coil tubing unit) implementing and overseeing drilling, completion, workover, and/or P&A operations.

- Minimum formal education requested: High school diploma.

- Basic knowledge of math and science (i.e. technical knowledge of hydraulics, fluid flow, fluid mechanics, mechanical design and materials engineering).

Preferred Qualifications/ Experience

- Problem-solving skills, analytical ability and mechanical aptitude.

- Excellent communication and leadership skills.

- Willingness to travel, both domestically and internationally, with the opportunity to see various operations and work with multiple mentors.

Your Benefits

An ExxonMobil career is one designed to last. Our commitment to you runs deep: our employees grow personally and professionally, with benefits built on our core categories of health, security, finance, and life.

We offer you:

- Pension Plan: Enrollment is automatic and at no cost to you. The basic benefit is a monthly annuity to be paid to you in retirement for the rest of your life.

- Savings Plan: You can contribute between 6% and 20% of your pay and are encouraged to enroll right away. If you contribute at least 6% to your savings plan, the Company will contribute a 7% match.

- Workplace Flexibility: We have several programs such as “Flex your Day”, providing ad-hoc flexibility around when and where you work, as well as longer-term programs such as leaves of absence and part-time work.

- Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans.

- Culture of Health: Programs and resources to support your wellbeing.

- Employee Health Advisory Program: Provides confidential professional counseling for you and your family, including tools and resources promoting mental health and resiliency at no additional cost to you.

- Disability Plan: Income replacement for when you cannot work due to illness or injury occurring on or off the job. Enrollment is automatic and at no cost to you.
